Maintenance Report — MNT-0094-007

Asset: WELL-0094 (SW-24 Well 094, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 07 Mar 2025 08:00 · Finished: 15 Apr 2025 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 929 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0094-0052 on 2025-03-06 Report written: 16 Apr 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0094-0052 showed the wellhead at 10.8 °C with the air at 9.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 37 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
